The approach enables robust execution of challenging motions including dancing and complex ground interactions in both simulation and real-world environments.
AI.conclusion: CoCo-InEKF provides a robust solution for state estimation in dynamic, contact-rich scenarios by leveraging continuous contact representations that capture the full spectrum from firm contact to directional slippage to no contact, validated through real-world deployment on a bipedal robot.

title: Pelican-Unified 1.0: A Unified Embodied Intelligence Model for Understanding, Reasoning, Imagination and Action
summary:
We present Pelican-Unified 1.0, the first embodied foundation model trained according to the principle of unification. Pelican-Unified 1.0 uses a single VLM as a unified understanding module, mapping scenes, instructions, visual contexts, and action histories into a shared semantic space. The same VLM also serves as a unified reasoning module, autoregressively producing task-, action-, and future-oriented chains of thought in a single forward pass and projecting the final hidden state into a dense latent variable. A Unified Future Generator (UFG) then conditions on this latent variable and jointly generates future videos and future actions through two modality-specific output heads within the same denoising process. The language, video, and action losses are all backpropagated into the shared representation, enabling the model to jointly optimize understanding, reasoning, imagination, and action during training, rather than training three isolated expert systems.
  Experiments demonstrate that unification does not imply compromise. With a single checkpoint, Pelican-Unified 1.0 achieves strong performance across all three capabilities: 64.7 on eight VLM benchmarks, the best among comparable-scale models; 66.03 on WorldArena, ranking first; and 93.5 on RoboTwin, the second-best average among compared action methods. These results show that the unified paradigm succeeds in preserving specialist strength while bringing understanding, reasoning, imagination, and action into one model.

AI.tldr: Pelican-Unified 1.0 introduces a unified embodied foundation model that uses a single VLM for both understanding and reasoning, combined with a Unified Future Generator to jointly predict future videos and actions, achieving state-of-the-art performance across VLM benchmarks, WorldArena, and RoboTwin without sacrificing specialist capabilities.
AI.motivation: Existing embodied AI systems suffer from modularity and isolation, with separate models for understanding, reasoning, imagination, and action. This fragmentation leads to suboptimal performance and computational inefficiency. The authors seek to create a unified paradigm that maintains specialist strength while enabling joint optimization of all capabilities.
AI.method: Pelican-Unified 1.0 employs a single VLM serving dual purposes: (1) as a unified understanding module mapping scenes, instructions, visual contexts, and action histories into shared semantic space; (2) as a unified reasoning module producing autoregressive task-, action-, and future-oriented chains of thought in a single forward pass. A Unified Future Generator (UFG) then conditions on the projected latent variable to jointly generate future videos and actions through modality-specific output heads within a shared denoising process. The model uses joint backpropagation of language, video, and action losses into the shared representation.
AI.result: Unification demonstrates no compromise in performance. Pelican-Unified 1.0 achieves 64.7 on eight VLM benchmarks (best among comparable models), 66.03 on WorldArena (first place), and 93.5 on RoboTwin (second-best among action methods). These results prove that the unified paradigm successfully preserves specialist capabilities while integrating understanding, reasoning, imagination, and action in a single model.
AI.conclusion: The unified paradigm succeeds in creating a single model that maintains specialist performance across all capabilities. This demonstrates that unification does not require compromising any specific task performance, and that joint training across understanding, reasoning, imagination, and action yields superior results compared to isolated expert systems. The approach represents a significant advancement in embodied AI by bridging the gap between perception, reasoning, and action in a single unified architecture.

title: Hand-in-the-Loop: Improving Dexterous VLA via Seamless Interventional Correction
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are prone to compounding errors in dexterous manipulation, where high-dimensional action spaces and contact-rich dynamics amplify small policy deviations over long horizons. While Interactive Imitation Learning (IIL) can refine policies through human takeover data, applying it to high-degree-of-freedom (DoF) robotic hands remains challenging due to a command mismatch between human teleoperation and policy execution at the takeover moment, which causes abrupt robot-hand configuration changes, or "gesture jumps". We present Hand-in-the-Loop (HandITL), a seamless human-in-the-loop intervention method that blends human corrective intent with autonomous policy execution to avoid gesture jumps during bimanual dexterous manipulation. Compared with direct teleoperation takeover, HandITL reduces takeover jitter by 99.8% and preserves robust post-takeover manipulation, reducing grasp failures by 87.5% and mean completion time by 19.1%. We validate HandITL on tasks requiring bimanual coordination, tool use, and fine-grained long-horizon manipulation. When used to collect intervention data for policy refinement, HandITL yields policies that outperform those trained with standard teleoperation data by 19% on average across three long-horizon dexterous tasks.

AI.tldr: HandITL is a human-in-the-loop method that blends human corrective intent with autonomous policy execution to avoid gesture jumps in high-DoF robotic manipulation, achieving 99.8% reduction in takeover jitter, 87.5% fewer grasp failures, and 19% better policy performance.
AI.motivation: VLA models suffer from compounding errors in dexterous manipulation due to high-dimensional action spaces. While Interactive Imitation Learning (IIL) can refine policies, it faces challenges with high-DoF robotic hands because of command mismatch between human teleoperation and policy execution, causing abrupt "gesture jumps" that disrupt manipulation quality.
AI.method: Hand-in-the-Loop (HandITL) blends human corrective intent with autonomous policy execution to seamlessly intervene during bimanual dexterous manipulation without causing abrupt robot-hand configuration changes.
AI.result: HandITL reduces takeover jitter by 99.8%, grasp failures by 87.5%, and mean completion time by 19.1% compared to direct teleoperation takeover. When used to collect intervention data for policy refinement, policies trained with HandITL data outperform those trained with standard teleoperation data by 19% on average across three long-horizon dexterous tasks.
AI.conclusion: HandITL effectively enables seamless human intervention in high-DoF robotic manipulation tasks, preserving manipulation quality and enabling better policy learning through its gesture-jump-free approach to interactive imitation learning.
